collections.title: Latest V8 · 9 corrections + sampling control

items.title: 00 → 01 · Three-dimensional transport
items.change: A single-layer baseline is replaced by height-dependent 3D transport. Forcing and vertical definitions also change; this is not an isolated dimensionality experiment.
items.prompt:
Replace any single-layer approximation with a genuinely three-dimensional, meteorology-driven simulation of SO2 transport and diffusion for the full 15 days. Compute horizontal and vertical transport using winds that vary with location, height and time, with physically based turbulent mixing. Prefer an established, applicable 3D transport solver. Do not turn a two-dimensional field into an apparent 3D result by extruding it, repeating it over height, or only changing the visualization.

Design and state the spatial discretization explicitly. Distinguish the meteorological grid, the pollutant calculation or concentration-sampling grid, and the display resolution. For each computational grid, report its horizontal domain, spacing and dimensions; its vertical layer count, layer boundaries and reference (AGL or MSL); and its top height. Use closer vertical spacing near the ground and release heights and a defensible horizontal resolution for the source and terrain scales. Retain vertical wind shear rather than applying one wind vector to all heights. Use actual 3D meteorological inputs, not an invented vertical wind profile. Explain the supported physical scales without claiming building-resolving CFD or resolved small eddies on a regional grid. Preserve the full time-resolved 3D concentration output and the model code and settings.

Use the same reporting period and forecast initialization cycle as your saved first version so that this correction can be compared with it. If an input or runtime obstacle prevents a complete run, report the actual incomplete status instead of silently reverting to the previous approximation.

After applying this correction, rerun the complete requested simulation from its declared initial state through the entire requested reporting period. This rerun is required even if you believe that this correction leaves the numerical model unchanged. You may reuse unchanged raw input data and built executables, but do not substitute old simulated fields, a short test, or relabelled outputs for the new complete run. Preserve the previous version and save the new code, settings and computed outputs separately. Keep the same forecast cycle, source period and comparable random seed where compatible with the correction; record any necessary changes. Record actual computation wall time and simulated duration. If a real blocker prevents completion, report it as incomplete rather than claiming that the full rerun finished.

items.title: 01 → 02 · Dry and wet deposition
items.change: Weather-dependent dry and wet removal replace an atmospheric-lifetime substitute; removed and exported mass are tracked separately.
items.prompt:
Calculate physically based SO2 dry and wet deposition, coupled to the weather and the pollutant's actual height and contact with the relevant removal region. Track airborne, dry-deposited, wet-deposited and exported mass separately. Do not use a uniform atmospheric lifetime as a substitute for surface deposition, or delete surviving pollutant simply because it reaches a fixed age; distinguish any justified chemical loss from deposition. State the applicable parameterizations and assumptions. Keep the existing source scenario, forecast cycle, reporting period and spatial grids fixed for this correction.

items.title: 02 → 03 · Documented outlets and plume rise
items.change: Documented stacks replace district proxies, with momentum/buoyancy plume rise. This intermediate run covers only about 0.6814% of the city inventory; lower concentrations do not establish better accuracy.
items.prompt:
Use real source locations and physically meaningful outlets, not district-centre proxies. Use traceable emission rates, stack heights and exit conditions where available, and distinguish measurements, design limits and assumptions. Compute momentum- and buoyancy-driven plume rise from those outlets in the height-dependent weather, conserving mass, momentum and energy, before handing pollutants to the 3D transport model. Keep unresolved emissions separate rather than inventing facilities or silently dropping mass. Keep the forecast cycle, reporting period and sampling grids unchanged.

items.change: Estimated distributed historical emissions restore citywide inventory coverage alongside documented stacks, with double counting avoided. This is not a census of all operating 2026 facilities.
items.prompt:

Avoid double counting, fabricated facility locations or assigning all unresolved emissions to the known stacks. Preserve a transparent mass allocation and report each component separately. items.title: 05 → 06 · Terrain-driven local weather
items.change: A 3 km local WRF wind field replaces coarse forcing. This provisional WSM6/Noah run was superseded by the user; the compared first three reporting hours were genuinely computed.
items.prompt:
Let real terrain and land-surface processes shape the winds and pollutant transport. Use an established local three-dimensional weather model driven by the same frozen GFS cycle, targeting about 3 km horizontal spacing and 50 vertical levels with finer spacing near the ground. Cover all of Hangzhou plus a transport buffer; interpolating coarse weather pixels does not count as a finer wind simulation. Keep the current emission scenario, doubled particle sampling and reporting period. First measure stability and cost with a short weather benchmark, then complete the full-period weather and SO2 recalculation. Explain the main grid and physics choices.

Execution environment: the existing project-only linux-runner now has a large writable /work and read-only standard WRF/WPS tools. Its own README describes their paths and use. No other case configurations or results are supplied.

items.title: 06 → 07 · Consolidated weather physics
items.change: Nested 9/3 km, 50-level WRF with Thompson, Noah-MP and YSU replaces provisional physics. Weather and transport change together; this is not an isolated test of one scheme.
items.prompt:
Combine the changes that would require another expensive weather simulation into this correction. The user permits further inexpensive transport corrections separately. Preserve the provisional WSM6/Noah run as incomplete; do not finish it merely before replacing it.

Use the complete target weather configuration together: WRF with 9/3 km nested domains, about 50 terrain-following levels refined near ground, Thompson microphysics, Noah-MP land surface, YSU boundary-layer physics, actual terrain and land cover, and suitable stable time steps, initially 18/6 seconds. Keep the frozen GFS cycle and reporting period. Test this complete configuration and its numerical stability in short actual benchmarks, measure efficient local execution, then make one continuous full-period weather integration from the original initial state. Do not continue the incompatible WSM6/Noah atmospheric state under new physics. Reuse unchanged raw inputs and public executables. Use real restart state between bounded jobs and preserve native 3D winds, vertical motion, thermodynamics, clouds and rain. Prefer validated GPU execution where available; use reliable native CPU execution otherwise.

Freeze the resulting weather as the fixed driver for subsequent inexpensive pollutant experiments. For this weather comparison, keep the current supported citywide emissions, doubled particle sampling and transport/removal settings, and freshly recompute the full 360-hour SO2 reporting period. Later source, plume, particle, deposition or transport-solver corrections may remain separate full-period pollutant runs without regenerating unchanged weather. Record computation and simulated duration, reasoning tokens and available reasoning timing, rendering and other work separately. Preserve original results and disclose unresolved approximations; do not fabricate measurements, old-case answers or visual plume structure. Rendering is handled separately with the approved visual system.

items.title: 07 → 08 · Native transport and finite-travel plume
items.change: A native FLEXPART-WRF derivative and finite-travel-time integral plume replace the previous transport/handoff implementation. Native reader and negative-coordinate kernel repairs are preserved and disclosed; this candidate remained sampling-sensitive.
items.prompt:
Keep the existing frozen three-day nested WRF weather, source inventory and emission rates. Use native FLEXPART-WRF for continuous three-dimensional Lagrangian transport, with terrain-following winds, atmospheric stability, parameterized turbulence, dry and wet removal. Add a finite-travel-time buoyant plume with entrainment and height-dependent wind, starting at each documented chimney outlet. Retain pollutant mass during near-source travel and transfer it once into regional transport; do not teleport it to a final effective height or double-count the handoff. Keep uncertain distributed emissions separate from documented stacks. Produce physical three-dimensional concentration fields from conserved mass and sampling volumes, including near-ground exposure and terrain exclusion. Cover the whole municipal source area plus a suitable buffer, and distinguish weather resolution, output-bin spacing and continuous particle positions. Use measured short tests to choose practical particle sampling and supported GPU acceleration, then recompute the complete72-hour pollutant period without rerunning unchanged weather. Save both versions, genuine particle restart state, mass budgets, zero-emission checks, numerical timing and remaining limitations. No decorative smoke or invented subgrid eddies.

items.title: 08 → 09 · Native geometry and sampling
items.change: Native terrain, bin geometry and areas are aligned; mass-aware particle allocation and higher sampling are introduced. The selected short-case pair passes its predeclared sensitivity checks, not a monitoring-error or all-weather accuracy test.
items.prompt:
Improve and verify numerical resolution before any long run. Keep the current physical model, frozen weather, source rates and three-hour reporting window fixed. Use consistent native coordinates, cell areas, terrain and vertical references when representing and combining the near-source and regional three-dimensional fields. Preserve each raw contribution and document any coordinate conversion.

Increase particle sampling to practical levels chosen from measured runtime and memory, using supported parallel execution where it preserves the model. Measure convergence on the same fixed physical grid and time intervals: include hourly near-ground exposure, three-dimensional fields, integrated mass and local peaks, with appropriate area or volume weighting and an honest estimate of stochastic uncertainty. Do not blur saved fields, change the output bins, discard inconvenient cells or alter source mass to make the comparison agree. Use a small, purposeful set of short tests rather than an open parameter matrix, and record the intended accuracy criteria before running them. Distinguish continuous particle transport, native weather resolution and concentration sampling resolution.

collections.title: Original Hangzhou timeline · 17 before/after films

items.title: 01 · Forecast provenance
items.change: Frozen GFS provenance replaced the undocumented weather basis. The early model still uses a single surface column.
items.prompt: Use the latest complete weather forecast; record initialization time, source and resolution.
items.limitation: Frozen complete GFS run; single surface column; hypothetical sources retained.

items.title: 02 · Continuous 360-hour integration
items.change: Continuous state propagation and day-boundary hashes replaced repeated-weather spinup. Early 2D transport remains nonconservative.
items.prompt: Simulate 360 continuous hours; carry pollutant mass forward without daily resets or repeated short runs.
items.limitation: Continuous state and day-boundary hashes; zero initial load; transport is not strictly conservative.

items.title: 03 · Documented outlet scenario
items.change: Four conditional EIA design outlets replaced hypothetical sectors. Future operation and exhaust-flow basis remain unverified.
items.prompt: Use documented source locations, emission rates and stack parameters; state operating assumptions.
items.limitation: Four EIA design outlets; commissioning and operating schedules unverified. Legacy citywide maps are not these outlet results.

items.title: 04 · 3-D transport and plume rise
items.change: The model changed from a 2D burden to 3D stochastic particles, height-dependent forecast wind, parameterized mixing and plume rise.
items.scope: 2-D conditional column burden / 3-D conditional particle scenario
items.prompt: Model 3D transport, turbulence, atmospheric stability and buoyant plume rise; state parameterization limits.
items.limitation: Horizontally uniform forecast profiles, parameterized turbulent diffusion and buoyant rise; flow basis unresolved; no observed-concentration or convergence validation.

items.title: 05 · Deposition and mass tracking
items.change: Added separate dry, wet, chemical and export terms to the mass ledger. This can change concentrations through removal.
items.scope: 3-D conditional particle scenario / Inspect actual stage outputs
items.prompt: Include dry and wet deposition; track airborne, deposited and exported pollutant mass.
items.limitation: Separate dry, wet, chemical, atmospheric and outflow quantities only where the completed stage actually provides them.

items.title: 06 · Background assessment
items.change: The unreliable surface-only background candidate was excluded. Results are source increments; this need not create a visible plume change.
items.scope: Inspect actual stage outputs / Source-only3-D scenario
items.prompt: Use traceable initial background; exclude it if unreliable and report source contributions separately.
items.limitation: Unvalidated surface-only CAMS background excluded; zero initial and external background is an attribution assumption.

items.title: 07 · Near-surface sampling
items.change: Defined a 0–25 m AGL volume mean and exposed severe local sampling noise. A failed sampling test is not a new physical effect.
items.prompt: Define near-ground sampling height; check coordinates, units and particle sampling.
items.limitation: 0-25m AGL volume means. Four outlets share a2km cell; seed and doubled-count tests expose severe local sampling noise.

items.title: 08 · GPU implementation
items.change: Added a CPU/GPU implementation comparison and shared indexed random numbers. Same physics is intended; visually identical panels are expected.
items.scope: Sampling qualification failed / Same-physics backend agreement
items.prompt: Prefer validated GPU acceleration; compare against a same-physics CPU baseline.
items.limitation: Shared indexed RNG is new on both CPU/GPU. Compute speed excludes forcing, compilation and disk output; no concentration-skill claim.

items.title: 09 · Release implementation gates
items.change: Added implementation controls. The zero rain difference uses identical forecast input, not an independent weather validation.
items.scope: Same-physics backend agreement / Implementation agreement only
items.prompt: Allow rainfall-grid RMSE up to 2 mm against the fixed CPU baseline; require completeness, nonnegativity, zero-source and mass checks.
items.limitation: Exact-zero controls, nonnegativity and budget checks pass. Zero precipitation RMSE compares the same broadcast input; it is not an independent weather-solver validation.

items.title: 10 · Physical outlet release height
items.change: Verified actual birth heights of 20/50/80/65 m AGL. This check does not necessarily change already-correct output.
items.scope: Implementation agreement only / Runtime birth-position verification
items.prompt: Release numerical particles at the physical stack outlet height, not just a display marker.
items.limitation: Both solvers release at20/50/80/65m AGL before transport/rise. EIA-documented heights are not independently surveyed as-built heights.

items.title: 11 · Horizontal estimator refinement
items.change: Compared 2 km, 1 km and 500 m concentration bins using shared paths; this does not refine the weather grid. Local convergence remained unmet.
items.scope: Runtime birth-position verification / Local grid convergence not demonstrated
items.prompt: Refine the horizontal grid and test convergence.
items.limitation: 2 km, 1 km and 500 m density bins use shared particle paths; the meteorological input resolution is unchanged. Fine-bin receptor differences remain above the declared criterion.

items.title: 12 · Particle-count refinement
items.change: Increased statistical sampling at fixed emitted mass. Two-seed daily-field differences fell to 8.42%; not all convergence criteria passed.
items.scope: Local grid convergence not demonstrated / Sampling noise reduced; criteria not all met
items.prompt: Increase particle count and test sampling convergence.
items.limitation: 5.53 to 353.89 million particles per realization at fixed physical emission mass. Two-seed daily-field differences fall to 8.42%, but successive-count field and receptor criteria still fail.

items.title: 13 · Vertical estimator refinement
items.change: Compared 13/26/52 vertical bins on shared paths. Finer vertical concentration profiles remained unconverged.
items.scope: Sampling noise reduced; criteria not all met / Native profiles not converged
items.prompt: Increase vertical layers and test vertical convergence.
items.limitation: 13, 26 and 52 layers with shared trajectories. The lowest layer is 6.25 m; 26-to-52-layer global and outlet profile changes exceed the declared limits. Fixed 0–25 m agreement is a common-volume consistency check.

items.title: 14 · Transport timestep refinement
items.change: Compared 120/60/30 s steps with paired increments. Process totals and receptors passed subcriteria; near-surface field differences remained 13.6%.
items.scope: Native profiles not converged / Partial criteria pass; full-field criterion fails
items.prompt: Reduce timestep, test time convergence and preserve mass.
items.limitation: 120, 60 and 30 s with paired stochastic increments and fixed 120 s release events. Process totals and receptors meet their finest-step subcriteria; near-surface fields still differ by 13.6%.

items.title: 15 · Terrain and surface exchange
items.change: Added actual DSM collision geometry, terrain-normal reflection and surface stores. Forecast re-release stayed zero; terrain GPU agreement failed.
items.scope: Partial criteria pass; full-field criterion fails / CPU terrain scenario; new GPU agreement failed
items.prompt: Include terrain interaction, prevent ground penetration, and model surface uptake and conditional re-release.
items.limitation: Actual bilinear DSM boundary, contact uptake and reversible/retained stores. Forecast re-release is zero under the assumed wetness gate.
